transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose things just got a bit out of hand lately. I took on this project for the historical society... kind of acting like I could run the whole fundraiser myself. 

I was just... starting all these quilt designs, calling volunteers, making schedules. I ended up promising deadlines I couldn't possibly meet. So... that's why I'm here.
During this time, did you feel unusually high or euphoric?

I suppose... yes. At first, I felt... well, almost glowing, I guess. Like every idea I had was just wonderful. But... if anyone questioned me about things, I got a bit snappish. I just... I acted like they were standing in my way.
During that time, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy?

Yes... I suppose so. For a while, I was only sleeping a few hours a night. I'd wake up early, just ready to sew or... or make phone calls. But... well, now it's different. I either lie awake worrying about it all, or I sleep late and just feel... worn out.
During that time, were you talking much more than usual?

I suppose I was. Um... in the committee meetings, I'd just start talking about... the quilt patterns, the budgets, how we'd do the publicity. I guess I was speaking rather quickly. I remember some of the ladies trying to get a word in, trying to interrupt me, but... I just kept going. It felt like if I stopped talking, I'd... I don't know. It just felt impossible to stop.
During that time, did you have any beliefs that others said were unrealistic or not true?

I don't know about... unrealistic. I just... I really thought my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map. It felt like... like I had finally found the one thing that only I could make happen. But... I suppose some people didn't see it that way.
During that time, were you hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?
No... no, I wasn't.
During that time, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like major trouble at work, financially, or in your relationships?

I suppose... things got difficult at home. My husband... he had to step in and take over the regular household routines. And... well, he had to deal with the historical society for me, too. I just... I stopped keeping my commitments. It got to where I... I just couldn't face the people who were waiting on me.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?
I... well, I suppose I have. There are times when things just feel... heavier. I don't really feel like doing much of anything.
During those times when things felt heavier, did that low mood last most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't exactly keep track of the days when it gets like that. It just... it feels like a while, I guess. I couldn't tell you if it was exactly two weeks or not.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I suppose... yes. It's been a long time. Ever since I let the orders fall behind and... well, when all those issues with the volunteers blew up. I've just been stuck in this... this low place. Feeling awful about it all. It's been... maybe nine months now.
During that low period, did you lose interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy?

I suppose so. I... I used to really enjoy checking on my garden, or working on my own quilt entries for the fair. But lately... I just look at the fabric, or the seed catalogs, and... I don't really feel much of anything. It just doesn't matter.
About how long did that period when you felt especially energized and driven last?
I suppose... maybe five months. That whole stretch with the historical society project... it went on for about that long. Before... well, before everything fell apart.
During that energized period, did you ever hear or see things that other people did not?
No. I... no, nothing like that. I didn't see or hear anything that wasn't there.
During this low period, have you had thoughts that life wasn’t worth living or that you would be better off dead?

I... well... I wouldn't do anything. I don't have a plan or anything like that. But... sometimes I just think... maybe it would be simpler if I went to sleep and just... didn't wake up. Then people wouldn't have to keep cleaning up the messes I make.
